## F-11: Mobile Dashboard Companion

### API-1 — Mobile bootstrap (aggregated read model)

`GET /mobile/bootstrap?since=<ISO-8601>` → one round trip returning: caller identity/scopes, projects (paged), portfolios, active runs with current stage, open HIL gates, recent failures, auto-mode escalations, run groups, plus `serverTime` and `snapshotVersion`.
**Rules:** read-only; the payload is composed exclusively of authoritative F-1…F-7 data; `snapshotVersion` is required for the next delta call.

### API-2 — Mobile views

`GET /mobile/views/{view}?cursor=` where `view ∈ projects | runs | run_detail | gates | portfolios | escalations | auto_mode`
**Rules:** each view mirrors desktop semantics with a reduced field set; no mobile-only state exists; every field is traceable to its owning feature's API.

### API-3 — Offline snapshot and delta sync

`GET /mobile/offline-snapshot` → last-known state bundle with `snapshotVersion`, `generatedAt`, and an explicit `staleAfter` (default 15 minutes).
`GET /mobile/bootstrap?since=<snapshotVersion>` → delta of changes.
**Rules:** offline snapshots are stamped `readOnly: true`; the client must display an offline badge and must not offer any write affordance while disconnected.

### API-4 — Push notification registration

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/mobile/devices` | Register device token `{ "platform": "ios|android", "token": "string", "locale": "en-US" }` |
| DELETE | `/mobile/devices/{deviceId}` | Unregister |
| GET | `/mobile/notifications` | In-app notification center (paged) |
| POST | `/mobile/notifications:read` | Mark read `{ "notificationIds": ["n_1"] }` |

**Rules:** notifications carry only object references and safe summaries — no secrets, no parameters, no rationale text; tapping a notification deep-links to the corresponding view; push is opt-in per category.

### API-5 — Mobile command delegation

`POST /mobile/commands:draft` → forwards to F-9 API-4 and returns an F-6 draft; the mobile client then calls F-6 API-2 preview and F-6 API-1 execute.
**Rules:** the mobile companion exposes **no** direct mutation endpoint of its own; every write path is F-6; `403` from F-6 is surfaced verbatim.

### API-6 — Device-bound session and security

`POST /mobile/sessions` → device-bound session `{ "deviceId", "biometricAssertion": "string|null" }` → short-lived access token + refresh token.
`POST /mobile/sessions:refresh` → rotate.
`DELETE /mobile/sessions/{sessionId}` → remote revoke.
**Rules:** tokens are device-bound and revocable per device; screenshots/parameters can be suppressed per project policy; a revoked device receives `401` on its next call and the client must wipe cached state.

### API-7 — Capability and degradation reporting

`GET /mobile/capabilities` → feature availability flags (AI available, voice available, streaming available, notifications available) + `degraded: true` with the affected surfaces listed.
**Rules:** the client must render degraded surfaces as read-only with an explanatory banner rather than hiding them silently.

## F-12: Test Management

### API-1 — Test case registry and versioning

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/test-cases` | List (`filter[projectId]`, `filter[tag]`, `q`) |
| POST | `/test-cases` | Create |
| GET | `/test-cases/{testCaseId}` | Read with current version |
| PATCH | `/test-cases/{testCaseId}` | Create a new draft version |
| POST | `/test-cases/{testCaseId}/versions` | Publish immutable version |
| GET | `/test-cases/{testCaseId}/versions` | List versions |

**Version body** `{ "assertions": [ {"kind": "equality|schema|regex|threshold|semantic", "target": "...", "expected": ...} ], "inputs": {}, "tags": [], "determinism": "deterministic|nondeterministic" }`
**Rules:** published versions are immutable (`405` on edit); a published case may be quarantined but not deleted if referenced by a plan; `determinism: nondeterministic` requires an explicit flake policy at plan binding time.

### API-2 — Suites

`GET|POST /test-suites`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /test-suites/{suiteId}`, `POST /test-suites/{suiteId}/members` (`{ "testCaseVersionIds": [] }`), `DELETE /test-suites/{suiteId}/members/{testCaseVersionId}`.
**Rules:** a suite references *versions*, never floating case ids; deleting a member only affects future suite runs.

### API-3 — Plans and stage/project binding

`GET|POST /test-plans`, `GET|PATCH /test-plans/{planId}`, `POST /test-plans/{planId}/versions`, `POST /test-plans/{planId}:bind`
**Bind request** `{ "projectId": "prj_1", "stageId": "stg_6", "trigger": "stage_entry|stage_exit", "requiredForAdvancement": true, "gatePolicy": { "maxFailures": 0, "allowWaivers": true } }`
**Rules:** a binding with `requiredForAdvancement: true` makes the plan's gate verdict authoritative for F-3 stage advancement; a stage may have at most one required plan, otherwise `409 conflict.invalid_state`.

### API-4 — Test execution

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/test-runs` | Start on demand `{ "planVersionId", "projectId", "scope": {...} }` |
| GET | `/test-runs` | List (`filter[projectId]`, `filter[planId]`, `filter[status]`) |
| GET | `/test-runs/{testRunId}` | Read with counters |
| POST | `/test-runs/{testRunId}:cancel` | Cancel |
| POST | `/test-runs/{testRunId}:retry` | Retry failed cases only |

**Rules:** pipeline-triggered runs are created by F-3 as a governed stage step and carry the originating `runId`/`stageId`; results are deterministic per case version + inputs; a retry never rewrites the earlier run — it creates a new one linked by `parentTestRunId`.

### API-5 — Results and evidence

`GET /test-runs/{testRunId}/results?cursor=` → per-case `{ testCaseVersionId, status, durationMs, assertions[] (actual vs expected), failureSignature }`.
`GET /test-results/{resultId}/evidence` → structured artifacts (logs, diffs, response bodies) with stable references and hashes.
**Rules:** a `failed` result must carry at least one failing assertion with actual and expected values; evidence is content-addressed and immutable.

### API-6 — Quality gate verdicts

`GET /quality-gates/{gateId}` → verdict derived from the bound plan run.
`POST /quality-gates/{gateId}:evaluate` → recompute (idempotent within the same evidence revision).
**Response** `{ "verdict": "pass|fail|waived", "planVersionId", "testRunId", "blockingFailures": ["tc_1"], "waivers": [], "evaluatedAt": "ISO-8601", "evidenceRevision": "evr_9" }`
**Rules:** the verdict is the only input F-3 may consume for governed advancement; recomputation against a different evidence revision produces a new immutable verdict record superseding the old one.

### API-7 — Coverage tracking

`GET /coverage?projectId=&artifactKind=&baseline=` → coverage percentage per pipeline artifact, uncovered artifacts list, and delta vs. baseline.
**Rules:** coverage computation is derived from authoritative result evidence; unavailable artifact inventory degrades to `partial: true` rather than erroring.

### API-8 — Regression and flakiness

`GET /regressions?projectId=&since=` → cases that passed in a baseline and now fail, with first-seen timestamps.
`GET /test-cases/{testCaseId}/flakiness` → pass/fail history, flake rate, `signature` clusters.
`POST /test-cases/{testCaseId}:quarantine` → `{ "reason": "string", "expiresAt": "ISO-8601|null" }`
`POST /test-cases/{testCaseId}:unquarantine`
**Rules:** quarantined cases are excluded from gate verdicts but still executed and reported as `quarantined`; quarantine always expires or is explicitly reviewed — indefinite quarantine is not representable.

### API-9 — Waivers and approval

`POST /test-waivers` → `{ "testCaseVersionId": "tcv_1", "planVersionId": "tpv_2", "reason": "string (>=20 chars)", "expiresAt": "ISO-8601", "approvedByUserId": "usr_7" }`
`GET /test-waivers?filter[planId]=` → active, expired, and revoked waivers.
**Rules:** waivers require the `test:waive` scope and a human approver (never an Auto Mode decision); waivers are time-boxed and appear in the gate verdict's `waivers[]`.

### API-10 — Reporting and audit

`GET /test-reports?projectId=&from=&to=&format=` → aggregated pass rates, top failure signatures, gate outcomes, coverage trend.
`POST /test-reports:export` → `202` + artifact reference.
`GET /test-audit?filter[objectKind]=&filter[objectId]=` → immutable trail of case versions, plan bindings, runs, verdicts, waivers, and quarantines.

## F-13: API-First Access

### API-1 — Versioning and contract publication

`GET /api/versions` → supported versions with `status: current|supported|deprecated|sunset`, `deprecationDate`, `sunsetDate`, and links to each contract.
`GET /api/v1/openapi.json` → machine-readable OpenAPI document for the version (also `?format=yaml`).
`GET /api/v1/changelog` → additive vs. breaking changes per release.
**Rules:** breaking changes require a new major version; a deprecated version advertises `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response headers on every call; contract documents are generated from the running implementation, never hand-maintained separately.

### API-2 — Client authentication and scope authorization

`POST /oauth/token` (authorization-code + PKCE, client-credentials, refresh-token grants) → `{ "access_token", "token_type", "expires_in", "refresh_token?", "scope" }`
`POST /oauth/revoke` → revoke a token or refresh token.
`GET|POST /api-keys`, `GET /api-keys/{keyId}`, `POST /api-keys/{keyId}:rotate`, `DELETE /api-keys/{keyId}`
**Rules:** secrets are returned exactly once at creation/rotation and stored hashed; scopes are least-privilege and mirrored from the operator's effective authorization — an API client can never exceed its owner's scope; `insufficient_scope` is returned as `403 auth.forbidden` with `error.details[].requiredScope`.

### API-3 — Uniform request/response envelope

Every operation in this document conforms to the global conventions block. This contract additionally guarantees:
- `GET` responses expose `ETag` and honor `If-None-Match` → `304`.
- `PATCH`/`PUT` require `If-Match`.
- `POST` commands require `Idempotency-Key`; a replay returns the original status, body, and `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; a replay with a divergent payload returns `409 idempotency.mismatch`.
- Errors always carry `requestId`; `retryable` is explicit on `429`, `503`, and transient `5xx`.

### API-4 — Asynchronous long-running operations

`GET /operations/{operationId}` → `{ "kind": "bulk_start|delete_project|export|deployment_upgrade", "status": "pending|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled", "progress": { "unitsDone", "unitsTotal" }, "resultRef": "...", "error": null }`
`POST /operations/{operationId}:cancel` → cooperative cancel.
`GET /operations/{operationId}/events` → `text/event-stream` progress.
**Rules:** any request that cannot complete inside 5 s returns `202` with an `Operation`; `resultRef` is a stable, scope-checked reference to the created/affected resources.

### API-5 — Streaming surface

`GET /api/v1/streams/{streamKind}` (`streamKind ∈ run_events | group_events | operation_events | audit_tail`)
**Rules:** `text/event-stream` with `id:`, `event:`, `data:` lines; `Last-Event-ID` replay is gap-free for at least 5 minutes; a `heartbeat` event every 15 s; `429` if a client exceeds its concurrent-stream quota; the stream never carries data the caller could not read synchronously.

### API-6 — Webhooks and event subscriptions

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET|POST | `/webhooks` | List / create subscription |
| GET|PATCH|DELETE | `/webhooks/{webhookId}` | Manage |
| POST | `/webhooks/{webhookId}:test` | Send a synthetic delivery |
| GET | `/webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries` | Delivery log with response codes |
| POST | `/webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries/{deliveryId}:redeliver` | Manual replay |

**Subscription body** `{ "url": "https://...", "eventTypes": ["run.failed","gate.opened"], "secret": "returned-once", "filters": { "projectId": "prj_1" }, "active": true }`
**Rules:** every delivery is signed (`X-PF-Signature: sha256=...` over the raw body with a timestamp header to prevent replay); at-least-once delivery with exponential retry; deliveries are ordered per `subscriptionId + objectId`; a failing endpoint is auto-disabled after a configured threshold and notified to the owner.

### API-7 — Bulk operations

`POST /bulk-operations` → `{ "operation": "create|update|delete|command", "resource": "projects|runs|test-cases", "items": [...], "atomic": false }`
**Response** `202` + `Operation`; results enumerate per-item `succeeded|failed` with an error per failed item.
**Rules:** `atomic: true` rolls the whole batch back on any failure; batch size cap per resource (default 500) exceeded → `422`.

### API-8 — Dry run

Any state-changing operation accepts `Dry-Run: true` and returns `200` with `{ "dryRun": true, "effect": { ... }, "warnings": [] }` and no persisted change. `Dry-Run` is honored on F-6 commands, F-4 bulk operations, F-12 exports, and F-15 upgrades.

### API-9 — Rate limiting and quotas

`GET /quotas` → `{ "limits": [ { "scope": "client", "metric": "requests_per_minute", "limit": 600, "used": 120, "resetAt": "ISO-8601" } ] }`
Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset`; `429` responses carry `Retry-After` and `error.retryable: true`.
**Rules:** streaming connections and bulk operations are metered by their own metrics; quota breaches are recorded in the API activity audit.

### API-10 — Capability discovery

`GET /api/v1/capabilities` → machine-readable list of enabled capabilities (features, optional subsystems, deployment-exposed surfaces) with the operation ids that implement each, so a client can adapt instead of probing.
**Rules:** discovery reflects actual runtime enablement (e.g. an air-gapped deployment reports AI/voice capabilities as disabled).

### API-11 — API activity audit

`GET /api-audit?filter[clientId]=&filter[operationId]=&filter[outcome]=&cursor=` → immutable record per call: actor, client, operation, target, outcome, latency, request id, and any scope denials.
**Rules:** read-only; retained per the deployment's retention policy; secrets never appear in audit payloads.

### API-12 — SDK / CLI generation and sandbox

`GET /api/v1/sdk/{language}` → generated client artifact reference (versioned alongside the contract).
`POST /sandbox/sessions` → ephemeral, isolated installation-scoped sandbox with the same contract and reset-on-request semantics.
`POST /sandbox/sessions/{sessionId}:reset` → wipe sandbox state.
**Rules:** sandbox credentials are distinct from production credentials and sandbox operations can never target non-sandbox resources.

## F-14: API Reuse and Extension Analysis

### API-1 — Contract inventory snapshots

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api-inventory/snapshots` | Capture a snapshot from the F-13 contract surface |
| GET | `/api-inventory/snapshots` | List snapshots (`filter[apiVersion]`, `filter[from]`, `filter[to]`) |
| GET | `/api-inventory/snapshots/{snapshotId}` | Read snapshot metadata and counts |
| GET | `/api-inventory/snapshots/{snapshotId}/operations` | Enumerated operations with signature, scopes, resources |
| GET | `/api-inventory/diff?from=&to=` | Added / removed / changed operations |

**Rules:** snapshots are immutable and read-only against F-13 — the analysis layer never mutates, deprecates, or publishes a contract.

### API-2 — Demand registry

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api-demand` | List registered demand items |
| POST | `/api-demand` | Register demand `{ "capability": "string", "consumer": "string", "area": "runs|projects|tests|...", "rationale": "string", "priority": "must|should|could" }` |
| GET | `/api-demand/{demandId}` | Read |
| PATCH | `/api-demand/{demandId}` | Update status/rationale |
| DELETE | `/api-demand/{demandId}` | Withdraw (soft delete, retained for history) |

### API-3 — Reuse analysis requests and results

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/reuse-analyses` | Run analysis `{ "demandIds": [], "snapshotId": "snap_9", "areas": ["runs"] }` |
| GET | `/reuse-analyses` | List analyses |
| GET | `/reuse-analyses/{analysisId}` | Read status, summary counts, coverage |
| GET | `/reuse-analyses/{analysisId}/findings` | Per-demand classification |

**Finding body**
```json
{ "demandId": "d_1", "classification": "reuse|extend|version|new",
  "matchedOperations": ["POST /runs/{runId}:retry"],
  "gap": "no per-stage retry on run groups",
  "confidence": 0.82,
  "conflicts": [ { "withOperation": "POST /run-groups/{id}:retry-failed", "kind": "overlap" } ],
  "recommendation": "extend" }
```
**Rules:** classification is one of the four fixed values — the analysis may recommend, it may not decide; low-confidence findings (`confidence < 0.6`) are marked `needs_review`; the engine is read-only against F-13 and produces no contract changes.

### API-4 — Duplication and overlap findings

`GET /duplication-findings?filter[area]=&filter[severity]=` → pairs of near-identical or overlapping operations with similarity score, the differing aspects, and a recommended resolution (`merge|alias|leave|deprecate_candidate`).
**Rules:** `deprecate_candidate` is advisory only — deprecation is F-13's lifecycle act, never F-14's.

### API-5 — Coverage scoring

`GET /api-coverage?area=&snapshotId=` → `{ "area": "runs", "score": 0.78, "coveredDemand": 12, "totalDemand": 15, "uncoveredDemandIds": ["d_4","d_9"] }`
**Rules:** the score is a derived, reproducible function of demand + snapshot; it is stamped with `snapshotId` so historical scores remain explainable.

### API-6 — Review and decision records

`GET|POST /reuse-decisions` → `{ "analysisId": "ra_1", "demandId": "d_1", "decision": "reuse|extend|version|new|reject", "decidedByUserId": "usr_7", "rationale": "string (>=20 chars)", "targetOperationId": "optional" }`
`GET /reuse-decisions/{decisionId}` → decision with the exact analysis revision it was based on.
**Rules:** decisions are immutable; a superseding decision references the one it replaces; a decision never itself modifies a contract.

### API-7 — Published reuse guidance

`GET /reuse-guidance?area=` → human- and machine-readable guidance: which operation to use for a capability, what is intentionally *not* offered, and the extension path for the remainder.
`POST /reuse-guidance:export` → `202` + artifact reference for a guidance snapshot.

## F-15: Deployment Options

### API-1 — Deployment target catalog

`GET /deployment-targets` → supported targets with guarantees.
```json
{ "id": "self_hosted_kubernetes", "name": "Self-hosted Kubernetes",
  "topologies": ["single_region_ha", "multi_region"],
  "sizingProfiles": ["s","m","l"],
  "guarantees": { "offlineCapable": true, "dataResidency": "operator_choice", "sla": "operator_defined" },
  "capabilities": { "ai": true, "voice": false, "notifications": true },
  "entitlements": ["enterprise"] }
```
`GET /deployment-targets/{targetId}` → full requirements: prerequisites, resource minimums, network/TLS/identity wiring, secret contract, supported upgrade paths.
**Rules:** the catalog is the single source of truth for what is supported; a deployment that does not match a catalog entry is reported as `unsupported` with the deviating fields.

### API-2 — Deployment records and provisioning

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/deployments` | Provision/bootstrap a deployment |
| GET | `/deployments` | List |
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}` | Read status and health summary |
| PATCH | `/deployments/{deploymentId}` | Update metadata/labels |
| POST | `/deployments/{deploymentId}:decommission` | Tear down |
| DELETE | `/deployments/{deploymentId}` | Remove the record |

**Provision request** `{ "targetId": "self_hosted_kubernetes", "topology": "single_region_ha", "sizingProfile": "m", "region": "eu-west-1", "configRevisionId": "cfg_2|null", "hardeningProfile": "baseline|hardened" }`
**Response** `202` + `Operation` with step-by-step progress.
**Rules:** provisioning is idempotent per `Idempotency-Key`; decommission requires `?confirm=<deploymentName>` and refuses while the deployment serves active runs unless `force=true`; the record is retained after decommission for audit.

### API-3 — Installation manifest

`GET /deployments/{deploymentId}/manifest` → the machine-readable manifest describing the running installation: deployment id, target, topology, sizing, component versions, enabled capabilities, feature flags, data-residency placement, entitlement binding, config revision, and build identifiers.
**Rules:** the manifest is the authoritative description of a running installation and is consumed by F-13 capability discovery; it is read-only via this API (changes flow through configuration revisions, API-4).

### API-4 — Configuration and secrets

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/configuration` | Current effective configuration (secrets redacted) |
| PUT | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/configuration` | Apply a new configuration revision |
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/configuration/revisions` | Revision history |
| POST | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/configuration/revisions/{revisionId}:rollback` | Roll back configuration |

**Rules:** secret *values* are never returned — only `{ "key": "...", "source": "vault|k8s-secret|env", "present": true }`; configuration is validated against the target's schema before acceptance (`422` with field-level details); applying a revision is a long-running operation when it requires a restart.

### API-5 — Upgrade and rollback

`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:upgrade-plan` → `{ "targetVersion": "1.8.0" }` → compatibility report (`blockers[]`, `warnings[]`, `estimatedDowntime`, `requiredBackups`).
`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:upgrade` → `202` + `Operation` (requires a cleared plan id).
`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:rollback` → `{ "toVersion": "1.7.3", "reason": "string" }`
`GET /deployments/{deploymentId}/upgrades` → history with outcomes.

**Rules:** upgrade is refused (`409 conflict.invalid_state`) if the plan reports unresolved blockers; rollback requires a compatible backup and returns `422` when the schema migration is one-way; every upgrade/rollback is recorded immutably with the executing actor.

### API-6 — Scaling, health, and parity

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/deployments/{deploymentId}:scale` | `{ "sizingProfile": "l", "componentOverrides": {} }` |
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/health` | Component-level health with `ok|degraded|down` and dependency status |
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/parity` | Capability parity vs. the target's catalog guarantees |
| GET | `/deployments/{deploymentId}/drift` | Detected drift from the declared configuration/manifest |

**Rules:** scaling is rejected if it would violate the target's data-residency or HA guarantees (`422`); `drift` findings are advisory and link to the exact deviating field; a `down` component reports its blast radius (which capabilities are unavailable).

### API-7 — Backup and restore

`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:backup` → `{ "scope": "full|config|data", "retentionDays": 30 }` → `202` + `Operation` + backup id.
`GET /deployments/{deploymentId}/backups` → list with verification status.
`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:restore` → `{ "backupId": "bkp_9", "confirm": true }` → `202`; restore is destructive and requires `deployment:restore` scope.
**Rules:** every backup is integrity-verified and reports `verified: true|false`; restore into a non-empty deployment requires `confirm=true` and is refused while runs are active unless `force=true`.

### API-8 — Observability and identity wiring

`GET|PUT /deployments/{deploymentId}/observability` → metrics/tracing/log sinks, sampling, retention.
`GET|PUT /deployments/{deploymentId}/identity` → identity provider wiring (OIDC/SAML/LDAP), group-to-role mapping, and session policy.
`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}/identity:test` → connection and mapping dry run.

**Rules:** identity changes are validated with a dry run before persistence; observability endpoints never expose credentials, only destination identifiers and health status.

### API-9 — Cost estimation and data residency

`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:cost-estimate` → `{ "sizingProfile", "targetId", "topology", "region", "usageAssumptions": { "runsPerDay", "avgRunMinutes" } }` → line-item estimate with a timestamped, deterministic basis.
`GET /deployments/{deploymentId}/residency` → where each data class (project, run telemetry, transcript/audio, audit, backups) is stored, with region and retention per class.
**Rules:** residency answers must enumerate every data class — an unknown class is reported as `unclassified` rather than omitted; cost estimates never mutate deployment state.

### API-10 — Air-gapped / offline delivery

`GET /deployment-targets/{targetId}/offline-bundle` → bundle manifest (version, checksums, size) for disconnected installation.
`POST /deployments/{deploymentId}:offline-import` → `202` + `Operation` applying a signed bundle.
**Rules:** bundles must be signature-verified; an unsigned or mismatched bundle is rejected with `422`; an air-gapped deployment reports AI/voice capabilities as disabled through F-13 API-10 discovery rather than failing at call time.

## F-16: Voice Reference Alignment

### API-1 — Reference registration and lifecycle

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/voice-references` | List (`filter[locale]`, `filter[status]`, `q`) |
| POST | `/voice-references` | Register a target voice `{ "name", "locale", "description", "intendedUse" }` |
| GET | `/voice-references/{referenceId}` | Read with sample and version summary |
| PATCH | `/voice-references/{referenceId}` | Update metadata (never audio) |
| POST | `/voice-references/{referenceId}:retire` | Retire |
| DELETE | `/voice-references/{referenceId}` | Delete (blocked if bound to a voice profile in use) |

**Rules:** a reference must resolve to exactly one locale; retired references remain readable for audit but cannot be bound or used in new synthesis.

### API-2 — Sample ingestion

`POST /voice-references/{referenceId}/samples` (`multipart/form-data` or `application/json` with a content reference)
**Request** `{ "segments": [ { "uri": "...", "transcript": "string", "startMs", "endMs" } ], "consentAttestation": true }`
**Response** `202` + `Operation`.
**Rules:** `consentAttestation: true` is mandatory — ingestion without it is rejected with `422 validation.field`; unsupported codecs/sample rates are normalized and the transformation is reported in sample metadata; a sample failing integrity checks is stored as `rejected` with a diagnostic, never silently dropped.

### API-3 — Preprocessing, alignment, and scoring

`POST /voice-references/{referenceId}:align` → `{ "sampleIds": [], "presetId": "default|null", "batch": true }` → `202` + alignment job id.
`GET /voice-references/{referenceId}/alignments/{jobId}` → job status and per-sample results:
```json
{ "sampleId": "smp_1", "status": "pass|review|fail",
  "scores": { "alignment": 0.94, "consistency": 0.88, "quality": 0.91 },
  "diagnostics": [ { "code": "low_energy_segment", "atMs": 4120 } ] }
```
`POST /voice-references/{referenceId}/alignments/{jobId}:cancel`
**Rules:** verdicts are objective and thresholded by the active preset; `pass` requires all scores at or above the preset thresholds; `fail` results are retained with diagnostics and are never counted toward a profile version; batch alignment is resumable and reports per-sample progress.

### API-4 — Alignment settings and presets

`GET|PUT /voice-alignment-settings` → thresholds, normalization policy, consistency window, and default preset.
`GET|POST /voice-alignment-presets`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /voice-alignment-presets/{presetId}`
**Rules:** changing thresholds never retroactively alters existing verdicts; a new verdict set is produced as a new alignment run tied to the preset version used.

### API-5 — Reference profile versions

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/voice-references/{referenceId}/versions` | Compose an immutable profile version from passing samples |
| GET | `/voice-references/{referenceId}/versions` | List versions |
| GET | `/voice-reference-versions/{versionId}` | Read version with composition and scores |
| POST | `/voice-reference-versions/{versionId}:approve` | Approve for use |
| POST | `/voice-reference-versions/{versionId}:retire` | Retire |

**Compose request** `{ "sampleIds": ["smp_1","smp_2"], "presetId": "default", "notes": "string" }`
**Rules:** composition accepts only samples with a `pass` verdict; versions are immutable (`405` on edit); only an approved version may be bound (API-6) or used by F-10; approval requires the `voice_reference:approve` scope and records the approver immutably.

### API-6 — Locale and Voice Companion binding

`GET|PUT /voice-reference-bindings` → mapping of locale → approved profile version, plus the resolution rule (exact locale → language fallback → platform default).
`GET /voice-reference-bindings/resolve?locale=en-GB` → the exact profile version F-10 would use, with the resolution path taken.
`POST /voice-reference-bindings:validate` → detects gaps, ambiguities, or bindings to retired versions.
**Rules:** only approved versions are bindable (`409` otherwise); an unresolved locale returns `404` with the attempted resolution chain so the failure is diagnosable; F-10 always resolves through this contract rather than selecting a profile itself.

### API-7 — Drift and cross-sample consistency

`GET /voice-references/{referenceId}/drift` → comparison of the approved profile against fresh samples: per-sample scores, drift verdict (`stable|drifting|diverged`), and the samples responsible.
`POST /voice-references/{referenceId}/drift:check` → run a check against newly ingested samples → `202` + `Operation`.
`GET /voice-references/{referenceId}/consistency` → intra- and cross-sample consistency with outliers enumerated.
**Rules:** `diverged` never mutates an approved version — it raises a review recommendation and optionally notifies per API-8; a new version must be explicitly composed and approved to take effect.

### API-8 — Preview synthesis, notifications, and failures

`POST /voice-reference-versions/{versionId}:preview-synthesis` → `{ "text": "string (<=500 chars)", "format": "opus|mp3|wav" }` → audio stream plus a preview id.
`GET /voice-references/{referenceId}/notifications` → completion, approval, drift, and failure notifications for the reference owner.
`GET /voice-alignment-failures?filter[referenceId]=` → diagnosable failure clusters with remediation hints.
**Rules:** preview synthesis is permitted for non-approved versions (that is its purpose) but is watermarked/labelled `preview: true` and may never be routed to a live Voice Companion session.

### API-9 — Search, import, and export

`GET /voice-references:search?q=&locale=&status=` → ranked search across references, versions, and samples with facets.
`POST /voice-references:export` → `202` + artifact containing references, versions, and bindings (audio exported only when policy permits, with consent provenance attached).
`POST /voice-references:import` → `202` + `Operation`; imported references arrive `unapproved` and must pass alignment and approval before binding.
**Rules:** export excludes rejected samples by default; import of a reference whose locale conflicts with an existing binding does not auto-rebind — it returns a conflict report requiring explicit resolution.

### API-10 — Role-gated access and audit

`GET /voice-references/{referenceId}/access` → caller's effective scopes (read, ingest, align, compose, approve, retire, bind).
`GET /voice-reference-audit?filter[referenceId]=&filter[objectKind]=` → immutable trail covering registration, sample ingestion (with consent attestation references), alignment runs and verdicts, version composition, approvals, retirements, binding changes, drift checks, previews, and imports/exports — each with actor, timestamp, and preset/version identifiers. Read-only; no mutation endpoint exists.

## Design Direction

Product Forge is an **operator console**, not a marketing site — its design direction is *mission-control calm under load*. The visual language is built on a dark-first, high-density canvas (a deep neutral base such as `#0E1116` with layered surface tones) so that the primary signal in any view — run status, gate backlog, stage progress, failure severity — is the brightest thing on screen, and nothing competes with it. State is never carried by colour alone: a consistent, semantically-locked palette (running = active blue, succeeded = affirmative green, blocked/failed = alert red, paused/waiting = amber, archived = muted grey) is always paired with an icon, a text label, and an ARIA-announced status so the same meaning survives colour-blindness, low-vision, and screen-reader use. Typography is a two-role system: a compact, tabular-figure monospace for identifiers, timestamps, stage numbers, run IDs and telemetry (so columns align and scanability is preserved at 10k-project scale), and a humanist sans for prose, labels, and conversation — the voice of the AI companion (F-9) and the operator's own notes. Motion is functional, never decorative: skeletons on first paint, subtle transitions on state change, zero animation on continuous telemetry streams, and full `prefers-reduced-motion` honour. The mood is *quiet confidence* — dense but breathable, information-rich without being noisy, and always showing the operator what the system is doing, why it did it, and what they can do next. Every surface in F-1 through F-16 composes from this one language so a portfolio roll-up, a live stage timeline, a HIL gate decision, and a voice-driven answer all *feel* like the same product, whether they arrive on a 34-inch control-room display or a phone in an operator's pocket.

## Components

> Owned by F-8 (Dashboard UX Component System) unless the row names another feature. Components are presentation contracts only: a component renders or emits intent, never mutates domain state. Every command-emitting component hands its intent to the manual command surface owned by F-6 for preview, confirmation, and audit. Local ids (`CMP-n`) are scoped to this section and do not collide with the `FR-`/`NFR-`/`US-`/`API-` ranges owned elsewhere.

### Component Layering

| Tier | Purpose | Owner | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| T0 — Design tokens | Colour, spacing, type, elevation, motion, density | F-8 | Semantic tokens only; no raw hex in feature components |
| T1 — Primitives | Single-purpose, unopinionated building blocks | F-8 | No domain vocabulary in names or props |
| T2 — Composed | Layout, feedback, data-display, command-safety patterns | F-8 | Reusable across ≥2 features; no domain fetches |
| T3 — Feature components | Domain-aware compositions for F-1 … F-16 | Named per row | Fetch only their own feature's published surface |
| T4 — Surfaces | Route-level assemblies (console, wizard, mobile shell) | Composed from T1–T3 | One surface per journey, not per feature |

### T1 — Primitives (F-8)

`CMP-1` `Button` (primary / secondary / ghost / destructive) · `CMP-2` `IconButton` · `CMP-3` `TextField` · `CMP-4` `TextArea` · `CMP-5` `Select` · `CMP-6` `MultiSelect` · `CMP-7` `Checkbox` · `CMP-8` `RadioGroup` · `CMP-9` `Toggle` · `CMP-10` `Slider` · `CMP-11` `Tabs` · `CMP-12` `Tooltip` · `CMP-13` `Popover` · `CMP-14` `Dialog` · `CMP-15` `Drawer` · `CMP-16` `Badge` · `CMP-17` `Tag` · `CMP-18` `Avatar` · `CMP-19` `Divider` · `CMP-20` `ProgressBar` · `CMP-21` `Spinner` (fallback only) · `CMP-22` `Skeleton` · `CMP-23` `KeyValueList` · `CMP-24` `CodeBlock` (monospace, tabular figures) · `CMP-25` `Timestamp` (locale-aware) · `CMP-26` `RelativeTime` · `CMP-27` `Identifier` (copyable monospace ID) · `CMP-28` `VisuallyHidden` · `CMP-29` `SkipToContentLink` · `CMP-30` `FocusRing`

All primitives ship keyboard contract (Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Escape, arrow keys in composites), a visible 2px focus outline, a 44×44 touch target on coarse pointers, and a mobile-safe variant.

### T2 — Composed Components (F-8)

**Layout & structure**
`CMP-31` `AppShell` · `CMP-32` `SideNav` · `CMP-33` `TopBar` · `CMP-34` `ContextBar` (current project/run/portfolio breadcrumb) · `CMP-35` `PageHeader` (title, status, primary actions) · `CMP-36` `Card` · `CMP-37` `Panel` · `CMP-38` `SplitPane` · `CMP-39` `StickyActionFooter` · `CMP-40` `ResponsiveGrid` · `CMP-41` `VirtualizedList` (10k-row registries) · `CMP-42` `SectionHeader` · `CMP-43` `CollapsibleSection` · `CMP-44` `Tabs`.

### Cross-Cutting Component Contracts

- **Rendering contract.** Every T3 component declares the authoritative feature surface it reads. No component infers domain state from a sibling component; F-8 renders, features own.
- **Real-time contract.** Live surfaces use `CMP-90`/`CMP-91`; on reconnect, stale renders are marked with `CMP-68`/`CMP-253` until a fresh frame arrives. Animations respect `CMP-102`.
- **Command contract.** No T3 component calls a mutation endpoint directly. It emits a command intent through `CMP-85`/`CMP-86`, is gated by `CMP-88`, confirmed per `CMP-77`/`CMP-181`, and echoed into the audit trail via `CMP-190`. This holds for keyboard, touch, chat-drafted (F-9), spoken (F-10), and mobile (F-11) origins identically.
- **State coverage contract.** Every list/table ships `CMP-60`, every mutation ships `CMP-74`/`CMP-75`/`CMP-77`, every async dependency ships `CMP-22`/`CMP-82`, every network boundary ships `CMP-76`/`CMP-61`. No surface may render an unhandled empty, loading, or error state.
- **Accessibility contract.** Status is always colour + icon + text + `LiveRegionAnnouncer`; `CMP-72`, `CMP-3`…`CMP-10` expose labels, descriptions, and `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`; composite widgets implement full keyboard semantics; RTL parity is verified for every T2 component via `CMP-101`.

## Data Models

> Scope: canonical domain and persistence model for Product Forge (features F-1 … F-16). Entity schemas are grouped by the feature that owns their lifecycle. Other sections reference entities by name only and never redefine fields. Local ids (`DM-n`) are scoped to this section.

### Conventions

| Rule | Definition |
|---|---|
| Identifier | `id` is a system-generated opaque, lexicographically sortable identifier (ULID). Never reused, never recycled after deletion. |
| Timestamps | `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `archivedAt`, `deletedAt` are ISO-8601 UTC with millisecond precision. |
| Optimistic concurrency | Every mutable entity carries `revision` (monotonic integer starting at 1). Any write supplies the expected `revision`; mismatch returns `409 conflict.stale_revision`. |
| Ownership | Every domain entity carries `ownerId` (principal reference) and, where authorization is scoped, `projectId`, `portfolioId`, or `runGroupId`. Missing scope means installation-wide. |
| Provenance | Every mutable entity carries `createdBy` and `updatedBy` (actor references). Immutable entities carry `auditRef` pointing to the command/decision record that produced them. |
| Deletion | Archived entities keep `archivedAt` and are hidden from default listings; permanently deleted entities keep a tombstone row (`deletedAt` set) so ids are never reused. Runs, decisions, test results, and audit records are immutable and are never deleted. |
| Sensitivity | Fields marked `[sensitive]` are encrypted at rest, redacted from list responses, and excluded from telemetry. Fields marked `[secret]` are write-only and never returned. |
| Cross-feature rule | A feature reads entities owned by other features through their published surfaces; only the owning feature writes. No shared mutable tables across feature boundaries. |

### Shared Value Objects

| Id | Name | Shape | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| VO-1 | ActorRef | `{ kind: user\|service\|system, id, displayName }` | all |
| VO-2 | TimeWindow | `{ from, to, timezone }` | schedules, reports, telemetry queries |
| VO-3 | Money | `{ amount, currency }` | cost estimation (F-15), budgets (F-7) |
| VO-4 | ResourceRef | `{ feature: "F-n", type, id, revision? }` | citations, audit, drafts |
| VO-5 | PagedList | `{ items[], nextCursor, total? }` | all list APIs |
| VO-6 | LabelSet | `{ key, value }[]` with key uniqueness | tags, labels |
| VO-7 | Approval | `{ decision: approved\|rejected, decidedBy, decidedAt, reason }` | gates, waivers, reviews |
| VO-8 | Locale | `{ language, region, script?, direction: ltr\|rtl }` | i18n, voice, references |

### Domain Entities

---

#### F-1 — Central Pipeline Control Plane

**DM-1 Project** — the lifecycle registry record at the centre of the control plane.

| Field | Type | Constraints / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | PK |
| name | string | 1–200 chars, unique within owner scope (case-insensitive) |
| description | string | ≤ 4,000 chars |
| ownerId | ActorRef | required |
| status | enum `ProjectStatus` | `draft \| active \| paused \| archived \| deleted` |
| portfolioId | string? | FK → DM-21 Portfolio (null = unassigned) |
| pipelineBinding | DM-5 PipelineBinding | required once activated |
| configurationRevision | integer | incremented on any configuration change; basis for run reproducibility |
| tierAssignmentId | string | FK → DM-14 TierAssignment |
| tags | LabelSet | |
| visibility | enum `Visibility` | `private \| team \| org` |
| seedIdeaId | string? | FK → DM-10 SeedIdea |
| archivedAt / deletedAt | timestamp? | life-cycle markers |

*Invariants:* status transitions follow `draft → active → paused → active → archived → active`; `deleted` is terminal and requires the project to be archived first. `pipelineBinding` is immutable once a run has executed against it; an upgrade creates a new binding revision.

**DM-2 PipelineDefinition** — a registered, named pipeline composed of ordered stages.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | PK |
| name | string | unique |
| description | string | |
| ownerId | ActorRef | |
| currentVersionId | string | FK → DM-3 PipelineVersion |
| status | enum `DefinitionStatus` | `draft \| published \| deprecated \| retired` |

**DM-3 PipelineVersion** — an immutable frozen snapshot of a definition.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | PK |
| pipelineDefinitionId | string | FK → DM-2 |
| versionNumber | integer | monotonic per definition |
| stageIds | string[] | ordered FK → DM-4 |
| publishedAt | timestamp | |
| publishedBy | ActorRef | |
| checksum | string | content hash, basis for reproducibility |
| status | enum `VersionStatus` | `published \| deprecated \| retired` |

*Immutability:* once published, a version is never mutated; changes create a new version.

**DM-4 StageDefinition** — a single stage in the 32-stage model.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | PK |
| ordinal | integer | position in the pipeline (1-based) |
| name | string | |
| kind | enum `StageKind` | `agent \| gate \| test \| deploy \| manual` |
| entryConditions | ConditionSet | evaluated before dispatch |
| exitCriteria | ConditionSet | basis for stage success |
| hilGatePolicyId | string? | referenced when the stage is gated |
| defaultTimeoutSec | integer | |
| retryPolicyId | string? | |

**DM-5 PipelineBinding** (value object embedded in DM-1).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| pipelineDefinitionId | string | FK → DM-2 |
| pipelineVersionId | string | FK → DM-3 (pinned, immutable) |
| boundAt | timestamp | |
| upgradePolicy | enum | `manual \| auto_within_major \| pinned` |

**DM-6 Run** — the registry record of one pipeline execution.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | PK |
| projectId | string | FK → DM-1 |
| pipelineVersionId | string | FK → DM-3 |
| label | string? | operator-supplied |
| status | enum `RunStatus` | `queued \| running \| paused \| blocked \| succeeded \| failed \| cancelled` |
| idempotencyKey | string? | unique per (projectId, key) |
| startedAt / endedAt | timestamp? | |
| planId | string? | FK → DM-15 RunPlan |
| parentRunGroupId | string? | FK → DM-25 RunGroup |
| trigger | enum `TriggerKind` | `manual \| scheduled \| auto \| api \| group` |
| triggeredBy | ActorRef | |

**DM-7 StageRun** — the per-run execution record of a stage.

### Relationship Map (cross-feature, read-only references)

| From | To | Cardinality | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| DM-1 Project | DM-21 Portfolio | many → 0..1 | membership edge is DM-22; F-1 writes the FK, F-4 owns DM-21 |
| DM-1 Project | DM-5 PipelineBinding | 1 → 1 | immutable once a run has executed |
| DM-1 Project | DM-14 TierAssignment | 1 → 1 | resolved via F-2 rules |
| DM-6 Run | DM-1 Project | many → 1 | owns no project fields |
| DM-6 Run | DM-25 RunGroup | many → 0..1 | parent link; F-5 owns DM-25 |
| DM-7 StageRun | DM-4 StageDefinition | many → 1 | plan fixes the version |
| DM-18 HILGate | DM-19 GateDecision | 1 → 0..n | decisions are append-only |
| DM-18 HILGate | DM-38 DecisionLedgerEntry | 1 → 0..n | present only when auto-decided |
| DM-30 ManualCommand | DM-30 (all mutations) | 1 → 1 | every mutation traces to exactly one command or ledger entry |
| DM-45 Conversation | DM-49 DraftCommand | 1 → 0..n | drafts are handed to F-6; never executed by F-9 |
| DM-50 VoiceSession | DM-45 Conversation | many → 1 | voice reuses F-9 conversation/grounding |
| DM-65 TestRun | DM-6 Run | many → 0..1 | stage-bound runs only |
| DM-67 QualityGate | DM-7 StageRun | many → many | gate verdict consumed by stage advancement (F-3) |
| DM-71 ApiContract | (any feature) | 1 → many | contracts describe operations; they own no domain state |
| DM-81 ApiInventorySnapshot | DM-72 ApiVersion | 1 → many | read-only projection (F-14) |
| DM-90 DeploymentRecord | DM-1…DM-114 | 1 → 0..n | one installation scopes all domain rows |
| DM-102 VoiceProfile | DM-48 Citation | many → many | spoken citations resolved from cited objects |

### Retention & Lifecycle Summary

| Entity group | Retention | Deletion semantics |
|---|---|---|
| DM-1, DM-21, DM-25 (registries) | until archived, then indefinitely until permanent delete | soft delete with tombstone |
| DM-6…DM-8, DM-17…DM-20 (execution) | run retention window (configurable, default 1 year) | immutable; never deleted |
| DM-19, DM-32, DM-38 (decisions/audit) | audit retention (default 7 years) | immutable; never deleted |
| DM-40…DM-44 (UX system) | current + prior published version | old themes retired, not deleted |
| DM-45…DM-49 (conversation) | per user retention setting (default 90 days) | user-initiated; drafts expire with conversation |
| DM-50…DM-54, DM-102…DM-114 (voice) | audio `ephemeral` ≤ 24h; transcripts standard | user-controlled; sensitive fields redacted on export |
| DM-55…DM-59 (mobile) | until device revoked | revoked devices drop caches immediately |
| DM-60…DM-70 (tests) | per project retention | results immutable; definitions versioned |
| DM-71…DM-80 (API) | active + deprecated versions until retirement date | published versions immutable |
| DM-81…DM-87 (analysis) | rolling 12-month snapshot window | derived; safe to prune |
| DM-88…DM-101 (deployment) | installation lifetime | records superseded, not deleted |
| DM-91 SecretReference | until rotation/revocation | value never persisted in any DM |

### Open Questions (data model)

1. **OQ-DM-1:** Should DM-17 TelemetryEvent retention be per-project configurable, or fixed by F-15 deployment policy? Currently modelled as a run-level window — needs an owner decision.
2. **OQ-DM-2:** DM-22 PortfolioMembership enforces one portfolio per project; if the user later wants multi-portfolio membership, the constraint must be relaxed by the user, not by this model.
3. **OQ-DM-3:** DM-105 VoiceProfileVersion depends on DM-19-style approvals (VO-7) — the approval workflow owner is not yet assigned between F-16 and a future approvals feature.
4. **OQ-DM-4:** Should DM-83 ReuseFinding reference a *demand* only, or also a proposed new API contract? Today it references demand only; extending it is additive and non-breaking.
